title: RefineResult
description: What a refine Smith writes to /work/out/result.json. The engine checks it (ReadResultDelegate) before its own rules; the Smith checks it with check-result refine. Strict types where the engine branches, any non-empty JSON where it only passes content on.

then.$comment: A filed ticket is pointed (bots/story-points.md): the engine refuses one without points.
21, 34 and 55 are a feature's (bots/story-points.md): anything else bigger than 13 is filed as a feature.

outcome.description: Branched on by the engine and the BPMN.

kind.description: Branched on: the flow the ticket starts.

featureMode.description: Branched on: the feature flow's mode.

userNamed.description: Branched on: the fields the user named in the ask or its answers. They bind, and the engine does not ask Jev about them. Optional.

blockedBy.description: Branched on: what the filed ticket waits on, each '#n' (a ticket in the intake's repo, or an earlier intake's ticket) or an earlier intake's id. The engine resolves an intake to the ticket it filed. Optional.

title.description: The issue title, filed as is.

body.description: The issue's markdown body; the engine reads its Allowed scope.

points.description: Branched on: the story-point estimate (bots/story-points.md); above 13 only for a feature; the engine requires it to file, and records it. A 'Points:' line in the ask binds.

repo.description: Branched on: for file and insufficient-permissions, the target repo (owner/name) the ticket belongs in when that is not the intake's own. Absent (or the intake's repo) rewrites the ask item in place; another registered target repo gets a new issue there and the ask item is closed with a link. A repo that is not a target repo is refused. Optional.

blocker.description: For insufficient-permissions (can't do with current permissions): the blocking challenge in 20 words or fewer, shown on the desktop ticket view's banner. Optional: the timeline derives one from reason when it is missing.

content.description: Passed on to a brief or a GitHub comment, never branched on: any non-empty JSON. A string is shown as itself; an object or array as a fenced JSON block.
